channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: Arias promotes in Madrid
item.description: Diego Sobejano has made partner at Arias SLP, the Madrid boutique founded by prominent Spanish arbitrator David Arias.

item.title: A&O Shearman partner goes solo in New Zealand
item.description: David Hume has left the partnership at A&O Shearman in Abu Dhabi to relocate to New Zealand, where he will practise as an independent arbitrator.

item.title: UAE group to proceed with claim against Lebanon
item.description: An Emirati conglomerate has said it will proceed with a US$1.7 billion investment treaty claim against Lebanon that it threatened two years ago over its inability to access funds deposited in the country’s banks.

item.title: Panel sides with Kazakhstan in oilfield dispute
item.description: An arbitral tribunal has reportedly ruled in favour of Kazakhstan in a multibillion-dollar dispute with the international consortium that operates the Karachaganak onshore oil and gas field.

item.title: New “global passport” allows hearing centre access
item.description: The International Arbitration Centre Alliance, or IACA, has launched a “global passport” allowing holders access to partner hearing centres around the world and use of their facilities and services.

item.title: Russian court orders Uniper to halt claim against Gazprom
item.description: A Russian court has ordered a Uniper subsidiary to halt a €45.2 million ICC claim it is pursuing against Gazprom’s export arm or else pay a fine.

item.title: Ecuador averts ICSID claim with release of pipeline guarantees
item.description: A Cayman subsidiary of Argentina’s Pampa Energía has dropped an ICSID claim against Ecuador after securing the release of guarantees worth US$100 million relating to the handover of an oil pipeline concession.

item.title: Partasides on the deterrent effect of contempt
item.description: In a speech in Houston, Constantine Partasides KC of Three Crowns considered “counter-insurgency techniques” to address party and counsel misconduct in arbitration and whether it is time to recognise “the arbitral equivalent of... contempt of court.”

item.title: Eni spars with partner over Sicilian gas field
item.description: A London and Tel Aviv-listed energy company says it is pursuing claims worth €265 million against its joint venture partner Eni in an arbitration over a gas field off the coast of Sicily.

item.title: Honduras to rejoin ICSID after Trump ally takes office
item.description: Honduras’ new conservative president Nasry Asfura has given notice of the country’s intent to rejoin the ICSID Convention – on the same day he was sworn in after narrowly winning elections with the vocal support of US President Donald Trump.
